headline: The site's services are healthy. Every Princess API call made by the 9 checked pages succeeded, including live cruise prices, deals, ships, ports and shore excursions. All open content APIs answered correctly and quickly, and most pages were usable within 1–3 seconds (the slowest, Alaska, finished loading at 8.6 seconds). The warnings are content and housekeeping problems, not outages: a leftover demo promotion in the navigation data, expired sales still in a lookup file, and a tracking script error on every page.

findings.Global header (navigation): The navigation data includes a demo promotion attached to the Packages menu item: title “Lorem Ipsum Dolor”, Latin placeholder text, and an image from a cfm-assets-demo folder. It was hidden in every menu we opened, but it is sent to every visitor on every page and would appear if that promotion slot were switched on. Fix: remove the promotion from the Packages menu item in the content system.
findings.Sale names: The sale-name lookup file still lists sales that ended on November 2 (Spooky Savings, Fly for Less, Free Onboard Spend). The site looks up names here, so this is low risk unless an old fare still carries one of these codes. Fix: confirm the file is cleaned up automatically after a sale ends.
findings.JavaScript errors (all pages): Every page throws n.includes is not a function inside Google Tag Manager's server-side service worker (/gtmfp02/). Visitors don't see it, but tracking that relies on that worker may be losing data. It was seen in automated Chrome and should be confirmed in a normal browser. Fix: ask the analytics team to check the GTM server-side container setup.
findings.Alaska destination: The Alaska region page was usable after 2.1 seconds but took 8.6 seconds to finish loading, the slowest of the pages checked. It loads two full-screen hero videos and 400+ requests. Fix: lazy-load the hero videos or use lighter poster images on first view.
